ATL.name: Asa Newell
ATL.note: Newell (toe) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Lakers.
ATL.long: Newell will miss a third consecutive contest due to a left great toe hyperextension. The second-year forward's absence will leave additional playing time for Luguentz Dort and Aaron Wiggins.

ATL.name: Keshon Gilbert
ATL.note: Gilbert (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Lakers.
ATL.long: Gilbert will miss a third straight game due to left knee inflammation. However, his absence shouldn't affect the rotation.

ATL.name: Jock Landale
ATL.note: Landale (hip) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Lakers.
ATL.long: Landale is in danger of missing a fifth consecutive contest due to a left hip strain. If the big man is unable to return Monday, Zuby Ejiofor figures to continue seeing increased burn.

ATL.name: Mouhamed Gueye
ATL.note: Gueye underwent surgery Tuesday to repair a fractured left foot that he suffered during a workout last week, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
ATL.long: Gueye will be re-evaluated by medical staff in 3-to-4 months, which means he'll miss all of training camp and preseason and likely the start of the 2026-27 regular season. It's a brutal blow for the fourth-year big man, given that the Hawks used the No. 23 overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft to select St. John's product Zuby Ejiofor. Gueye's absence means Ejiofor will have more opportunities in the preseason, and the rookie could establish a key role off the bench behind Onyeka Okongwu and projected backup center Jock Landale (ankle).

ATL.name: Henri Veesaar
ATL.note: Veesaar was diagnosed with a torn right ACL and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season, the Hawks announced Monday.
ATL.long: Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

BKN.name: Mikel Brown Jr.
BKN.note: Brown, who finished with 18 points (5-13 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 5-7 FT), one rebound, three assists and one steal over 25 minutes in Saturday's 124-121 loss to Atlanta, won't play in Sunday's game against Dallas, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
BKN.long: Brown logged his fifth consecutive double-digit scoring performance Saturday. However, his efforts weren't enough to help the Nets hold off a late Hawks comeback and earn their third win of the 2026-27 campaign. Head coach Jordi Fernandez mentioned after the game that the rookie won't suit up Sunday versus the Mavericks, the second game of a back-to-back. Without Brown in the lineup, Terance Mann should see more minutes off the bench. Keon Ellis, who didn't get on the floor versus Atlanta, might also get involved.

BKN.name: Grant Nelson
BKN.note: Nelson signed a two-way contract with the Nets on Friday, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
BKN.long: Nelson appeared in four regular-season games for the Nets during the 2025-26 campaign and will link up with the franchise again. He's expected to spend the bulk of his time with their G League affiliate to open the season.

BKN.name: Egor Demin
BKN.note: The Nets exercised Demin's third-year team option for the 2027-28 season, Sharif Phillips-Keaton of USA Today reports Thursday.
BKN.long: Brooklyn's decision keeps Demin under contract through the 2027-28 campaign as the organization continues investing in its young backcourt. The move provides additional long-term stability but doesn't directly impact his immediate fantasy outlook. Demin is currently dealing with a right leg bone bruise and is scheduled to be re-evaluated in one week.

CHA.name: Grant Williams
CHA.note: Williams (hamstring) is out for Monday's game against the Cavaliers.
CHA.long: Williams has yet to appear in a game this season due to a right hamstring strain. His next opportunity to suit up comes Thursday against the Suns.

CHA.name: Kon Knueppel
CHA.note: Knueppel (hamstring) was diagnosed with a left hamstring strain Sunday and will be re-evaluated in four weeks.
CHA.long: Knueppel missed the first eight games of the 2026-27 campaign. He returned for the 114-104 loss to Brooklyn on Wednesday, though he exited the contest after just six minutes of work and didn't return. With Knueppel out of commission for at least a month, Grayson Allen and Sion James are candidates to replace him in the starting lineup, especially with Dennis Schroder (hamstring) sidelined for a minimum of two weeks.
CHA.story: Hornets' Kon Knueppel out at least 4 weeks with latest hamstring strain

CHA.name: Moussa Diabate
CHA.note: Diabate (quadriceps) is questionable for Monday's game against the Cavaliers.
CHA.long: Diabate could miss a second straight game due to a right quad injury. If he is unavailable, Ryan Kalkbrenner could see extra minutes.

CHA.name: Dennis Schroder
CHA.note: Schroder has been diagnosed with a left hamstring strain and will be reevaluated in two weeks, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
CHA.long: Schroder, who missed Friday's game due to what was described as a left thigh injury, has been diagnosed with a hamstring strain. He is set to be reevaluated in two weeks, suggesting he will miss at least the next five games. Christian Anderson and Sion James could see extra minutes with Schroder sidelined.

CHA.name: Brandon Miller
CHA.note: Miller (groin) is listed as out for Monday's game against Cleveland.
CHA.long: Miller suffered a groin injury in Friday's 119-80 loss to the Celtics and didn't return. More information on his condition is expected to be released by Monday. For now, Tidjane Salaun and Sion James are candidates to replace Miller in the starting lineup versus the Cavaliers.

CHI.name: Norman Powell
CHI.note: Powell (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the 76ers, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
CHI.long: Powell was a late addition to the injury report Sunday morning due to right shoulder inflammation and soreness, and he'll miss his first game of the season. The veteran swingman's next chance to play will come Wednesday against the Spurs. Isaac Okoro will get the starting nod in Powell's stead. Additionally, Buddy Hield and Tre Jones could also see increased minutes.

CHI.name: Zach Collins
CHI.note: Collins (illness) is out for Sunday's game against Philadelphia.
CHI.long: Collins left Wednesday's 135-105 loss to the Knicks with an illness, then missed Friday's practice due to the ailment. He's battling a respiratory issue that will force him to miss his third contest of the season. Noa Essengue, Leonard Miller and Patrick Williams could all see additional minutes versus the 76ers with Collins out.

CLE.name: Sam Merrill
CLE.note: Merrill (elbow) is listed as out for Monday's game against the Hornets.
CLE.long: Merrill exited Friday's meeting with the 76ers because of a nagging elbow issue and didn't play in Saturday's 109-79 loss to the Knicks, marking his first absence of the 2026-27 campaign. With the 30-year-old now out for a second consecutive game, it should mean more minutes for Mario Hezonja, Meleek Thomas and Tyrese Proctor.

CLE.name: Jarrett Allen
CLE.note: Allen (knee) is questionable for Monday's game against Charlotte.
CLE.long: Allen has missed the last two contests due to a bruised right knee. Sam Merrill (elbow) is also sidelined, so Meleek Thomas may remain in the starting lineup, with Peyton Watson sliding over to the four and Evan Mobley handling things at the five.

CLE.name: Jaylon Tyson
CLE.note: Tyson (ankle) is out for Monday's game against the Hornets.
CLE.long: Tyson will miss a sixth straight game due to a right ankle injury. Tyrese Proctor and Meleek Thomas could retain larger roles with Tyson sidelined.

DAL.name: Sergio de Larrea
DAL.note: De Larrea (knee) is out for Friday's game against Utah.
DAL.long: De Larrea continues to miss time with a right knee strain, and it's not clear at this time where he's at in his rehab. He can be considered week-to-week until further notice.

DAL.name: Tarik Biberovic
DAL.note: Biberovic (heel) is listed as out for Monday's game against Sacramento.
DAL.long: Biberovic has been battling inflammation in his right heel, preventing him from making his NBA debut. While the rookie should be considered week-to-week, he likely has a way to go before earning a meaningful role in Dallas even when he's cleared to suit up.

DAL.name: Dereck Lively II
DAL.note: Lively (foot) is listed as out for Monday's game against the Kings.
DAL.long: Although there haven't been any negative reports regarding Lively's rehab progress, it doesn't appear he will be back in the lineup anytime soon. For now, the 22-year-old should be considered week-to-week. While Lively remains on the shelf, Daniel Gafford and Moussa Cisse should continue to handle most of the work at the five. Santi Aldama (knee) might also get involved in that area once he's cleared to return.

DEN.name: Cameron Johnson
DEN.note: Johnson (lower body) is questionable for Monday's game against Houston.
DEN.long: Johnson has already missed three games this season. If he is unavailable for a fourth time Monday versus the Rockets, it could mean more minutes for Spencer Jones and Alpha Diallo.

DEN.name: DeMar DeRozan
DEN.note: DeRozan is questionable for Monday's game against the Rockets due to lower back spasms.
DEN.long: DeRozan missed Wednesday's game against the Raptors due to back spasms, which now has him questionable for Monday's contest. If he is unable to go, Alpha Diallo, Bryce Hopkins and Trevon Brazile are candidates for increased minutes.

DEN.name: Christian Braun
DEN.note: Braun (calf/illness) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against Houston.
DEN.long: Braun is under the weather and also dealing with a left calf contusion. Nikola Jokic (elbow), Jamal Murray (shin), Aaron Gordon (lower body), Cameron Johnson (lower body) and DeMar DeRozan (back) are all listed as questionable as well, so the Nuggets could be shorthanded Monday. If Braun is ruled out, Spencer Jones, Cam Whitmore and Bryce Hopkins would be candidates for increased minutes.

DEN.name: Jamal Murray
DEN.note: Murray is questionable for Monday's game against the Rockets due to a left shin contusion.
DEN.long: Murray could miss his first game of the season due to a right lower leg injury. If he is unavailable, Tyus Jones could see an expanded role.

DEN.name: Aaron Gordon
DEN.note: Gordon (lower body injury management) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Rockets.
DEN.long: Along with Nikola Jokic (elbow), Jamal Murray (shin), Christian Braun (calf/illness), Cameron Johnson (lower body) and DeMar DeRozan (back), Gordon is questionable to play Monday. If the veteran forward is unable to go, Trevon Brazile, Spencer Jones and Alpha Diallo would be candidates for increased playing time.

DEN.name: Nikola Jokic
DEN.note: Jokic (elbow) is listed as questionable for Monday's game in Houston.
DEN.long: Jokic nearly had a triple-double in Saturday's 114-102 win over the Pacers. However, he's now in danger of missing his first game of the 2026-27 season due to a right elbow sprain. If Jokic isn't available to suit up, Marvin Bagley would presumably take his place in the starting lineup.

DEN.name: Julian Strawther
DEN.note: Strawther (knee) was diagnosed with a left knee sprain Friday and will be re-evaluated in six weeks, Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette reports.
DEN.long: Strawther suffered the injury in Wednesday's preseason game against the Clippers. The 24-year-old has appeared in 172 regular-season games for the Nuggets since entering the league in 2023, averaging 7.1 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 16.2 minutes per contest. He was in line to compete for an expanded role during the 2026-27 campaign. While that may be the case once Strawther is cleared to suit up, Tyus Jones and potentially Ryan Nembhard are candidates to receive more minutes in the interim.

DET.name: Jalen Duren
DET.note: Duren (hamstring) has begun on-court activity and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
DET.long: Duren is progressing in his rehab after suffering a right hamstring strain Oct. 23, though he'll remain on the inactive list for at least the next two weeks while ramping up toward a return to game action. Paul Reed should continue to play a sizable role in Duren's stead.
DET.story: Jalen Duren to miss at least two more weeks with hamstring injury

DET.name: Isaiah Joe
DET.note: Joe (hip) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lakers.
DET.long: Joe is still bothered by the right hip contusion he suffered against the 76ers on Oct. 25, and it will cause him to miss a sixth consecutive game Sunday. He'll have another chance to return to action Monday against Washington.

GSW.name: Will Richard
GSW.note: Richard is out for Monday's game against the Pelicans due to a left thumb UCL tear.
GSW.long: Richard will miss his first game of the season due to a left thumb injury. Gary Payton and Georges Niang could see extra minutes in his absence.
GSW.story: Golden State Warriors guard Will Richard sidelined with torn ligament in thumb

GSW.name: Gui Santos
GSW.note: Santos (knee) is listed as probable for Monday's game against New Orleans.
GSW.long: Santos' knee issue isn't anything new, so he'll be on the floor Monday, barring a setback. The 24-year-old has appeared in seven regular-season games in 2026-27, averaging 6.6 points, 3.6 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 18.9 minutes per contest.

GSW.name: Kristaps Porzingis
GSW.note: Porzingis announced on his social media that he's stepping away from basketball.
GSW.long: Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

GSW.name: Moses Moody
GSW.note: Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
GSW.long: Moody has been limited to individual court work, but team sources indicate he's ahead of Jimmy Butler (knee) in the rehabilitation process and is expected to return before the veteran forward. The 24-year-old still has several recovery checkpoints to complete, and Golden State has not established an official timetable. His eventual return would help replenish a Warriors wing rotation that will open the season without both Moody and Butler.

GSW.name: Jimmy Butler III
GSW.note: Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
GSW.long: Butler, who underwent surgery after suffering the injury Jan. 19, has progressed to individual court work but still has several rehabilitation milestones to clear. His next step involves landing comfortably after a game-speed jump. Coach Steve Kerr is hopeful Butler can rejoin Golden State for the latter portion of the season, though no official return date has been announced. The 37-year-old forward remains a significant part of the Warriors' plans and could provide a substantial boost during the second half of the campaign.

HOU.name: Clint Capela
HOU.note: Capela (ankle) is listed as out for Monday's game against Denver.
HOU.long: Capela will miss his fourth consecutive game Monday, meaning his next opportunity to return will come Wednesday versus Golden State. With Steven Adams (calf) also sidelined, Jabari Smith will likely continue to spend more time at the five behind Alperen Sengun. Oscar Tshiebwe may also see a few extra minutes of work.

HOU.name: Steven Adams
HOU.note: Head coach Ime Udoka said Wednesday that Adams (calf) is still without a timetable to return and will be evaluated on a "weekly basis," Varun Shankar of the Houston Chronicle reports.
HOU.long: Adams hasn't played since Oct. 23 due to a right soleus strain and remains without a definitive timetable to return. Oscar Tshiebwe figures to see increased burn until Capela (ankle) or Adams returns.

IND.name: T.J. McConnell
IND.note: McConnell is questionable for Monday's game against the Mavericks due to a right hamstring strain.
IND.long: McConnell missed the first nine games of the season due to a hamstring injury, which could hold him out for Monday's contest. If he is unavailable, Quenton Jackson is expected to see an expanded role.

IND.name: Tyrese Haliburton
IND.note: Haliburton (hamstring) is progressing well but does not have a timetable to return, Dustin Dopirak of The Indianapolis Star reports.
IND.long: Haliburton continues to recover from a left hamstring strain he picked up after Indiana's 110-102 loss to Milwaukee on Oct. 26. The Pacers star has missed the last five games, and his timetable to return is "uncertain", per head coach Rick Carlisle. Andrew Nembhard has been solid as the starting point guard with Haliburton sidelined, while Braden Smith and Quenton Jackson have provided extra depth in the backcourt. Indiana will get some reinforcements Saturday, however, as T.J. McConnell (hamstring) is expected to make his season debut in the NBA's Mexico City Game against the Nuggets.

IND.name: Johnny Furphy
IND.note: Furphy (knee) is practicing with the G League's Noblesville Boom, per Alex Golden of SI.com.
IND.long: The Pacers have been pretty quiet regarding Furphy's ACL recovery since the offseason, but it's encouraging to hear some form of progress as the forward begins to ramp up his activity. Although Furphy still lacks a firm timetable for a return and is likely to be brought back slowly, it appears a season debut before the start of the new calendar year is in the cards.

IND.name: Ben Sheppard
IND.note: Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
IND.long: Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

LAC.name: Isaiah Jackson
LAC.note: Jackson (groin) won't suit up for Sunday's game against the Pelicans, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
LAC.long: Jackson played through the groin issue in Wednesday's 117-116 loss to the Heat, but logged a season-low 13 minutes, suggesting the injury was bothering him. For now, Jackson should be considered questionable for Tuesday's game in Phoenix. Baba Miller will serve as the backup center with Jackson sidelined Sunday.

LAC.name: Brandon Ingram
LAC.note: Ingram (Achilles) won't play in Sunday's game against New Orleans, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
LAC.long: Ingram hasn't played yet this season. While the veteran is reportedly moving in a positive direction, he won't make his 2026-27 campaign debut Sunday versus his former team. Ingram's next opportunity to suit up will come Tuesday in Phoenix. In the meantime, Darius Garland will remain the Clippers' No. 1 scoring option.

LAC.name: Yanic Konan Niederhauser
LAC.note: The Clippers recalled Niederhauser (foot) from the G League's San Diego Clippers on Sunday.
LAC.long: Niederhauser remains unlikely to play a meaningful role in the short term following a seven-month recovery from foot surgery. The 23-year-old might instead make a phased return to action, possibly seeing limited minutes at some point in upcoming weeks and making some appearances in the G League. Last season, he averaged 4.3 points, 2.9 rebounds and 0.3 assists per regular-season game during his rookie year.

LAC.name: Bradley Beal
LAC.note: Beal (knee) will not be ready for the start of the regular season, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
LAC.long: Beal is dealing with knee inflammation that will keep him sidelined for Opening Night. While it's unclear how long the Clippers will be without the veteran guard, Darius Garland, Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn should dominate the backcourt minutes in his absence. Beal's 2025-26 campaign was cut short by a hip injury after he averaged 8.2 points and 1.7 assists in 20.6 minutes across just six regular-season appearances.

LAC.name: Jordan Miller
LAC.note: Miller underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn left rotator cuff and will be re-evaluated in six months, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
LAC.long: It's a tough break for Miller, who had an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during training camp in the fall. The timeline for a return is likely to keep him on the shelf until after the All-Star break. Miller's extended stay on the sidelines gives Kobe Sanders a chance to crack the Clippers' rotation.

LAL.name: Luka Doncic
LAL.note: Doncic has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Detroit due to lower-back tightness, Trevor Lane of LakersNation.com reports.
LAL.long: Doncic will be held out of the front end of this back-to-back set, with his next chance to suit up coming Monday at Atlanta. With the superstar floor general sidelined, Austin Reaves will likely see increased scoring and playmaking duties, while Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton could see an uptick in minutes.
LAL.story: Luka Doncic to sit out vs. Pistons due to lower back tightness

LAL.name: Quentin Grimes
LAL.note: Grimes (finger) did not return to Sunday's game against the Pistons.
LAL.long: Grimes went back to the locker room in the fourth quarter due to an apparent finger injury and was unable to return. He should be considered questionable at best for Monday's game against the Hawks.

MEM.name: Scotty Pippen Jr.
MEM.note: Pippen (back) won't play in Monday's game versus the Raptors.
MEM.long: It will be a fifth consecutive absence for Pippen, who has been sidelined by back soreness. His next opportunity to play will come Wednesday against Denver. In the meantime, Cam Spencer is in line for more minutes.

MEM.name: Isaiah Stewart
MEM.note: Stewart (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Toronto.
MEM.long: Stewart will miss a second consecutive contest due to a right knee bone bruise, and his next chance to play will come Wednesday against Denver. With the big man sidelined, Quinten Post will likely see increased minutes.

MEM.name: Richie Saunders
MEM.note: Saunders signed a two-way contract with the Grizzlies on Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
MEM.long: Saunders is still on the mend from a torn right ACL that he suffered during his final year at BYU. However, he has been cleared for on-court activities and will be allowed to practice with the Grizzlies now that he's officially signed with the team.

MIL.name: Gary Trent Jr.
MIL.note: Trent (illness) won't play in Sunday's game versus the Celtics.
MIL.long: Trent will miss his fourth consecutive game Sunday. However, since he has totaled only 13 minutes in his two appearances this season, his absence won't have much of an effect on the rotation.

MIN.name: Anthony Edwards
MIN.note: Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced.
MIN.long: Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.

MIN.name: Donte DiVincenzo
MIN.note: DiVincenzo (Achilles) remains confident that he'll return during the 2026-27 season, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
MIN.long: DiVincenzo is approaching six months since tearing his right Achilles during the first round of the playoffs and has been rehabbing with the expectation that he'll play at some point this season. The veteran guard has sought advice from Jayson Tatum, Tyrese Haliburton and Damian Lillard during his recovery, though Minnesota has yet to establish a timetable for his return.

NOP.name: Yves Missi
NOP.note: Missi (knee) is out for Friday's game against Minnesota.
NOP.long: Missi has been sidelined since picking up his injury Oct. 23. He remains without a timetable to return.

NYK.name: Josh Hart
NYK.note: Hart is out for Saturday's game against the Cavaliers due to right ankle soreness.
NYK.long: Hart practiced Friday, per Steve Popper of Newsday, but he's getting a bit more time to recover. Landry Shamet should draw a second consecutive start for the Knicks on Saturday.

OKC.name: Jaylin Williams
OKC.note: Williams (back) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Wizards, Brandon Rahbar of DailyThunder.com reports.
OKC.long: Williams will miss a third straight game due to lower-back spasms, leaving the door open for Micah Peavy, Kenrich Williams and Aday Mara to continue working in elevated roles Saturday. Williams' next opportunity to play will come Tuesday at Portland.

OKC.name: Thomas Sorber
OKC.note: Sorber (knee) is out for Wednesday's game against the Cavaliers.
OKC.long: Sorber remains in recovery mode due to knee surgery. Until the Thunder update his timetable for a return, Sorber can be deemed week-to-week.

OKC.name: Cason Wallace
OKC.note: Wallace underwent surgery Friday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
OKC.long: Wallace is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. However, there's still a chance he will return late in the campaign after sustaining the shoulder injury in Sunday's win over the Clippers. With Jalen Williams (leg) also set to be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Alex Caruso (ankle) should see significant playing time once cleared to return. In the meantime, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix are expected to see increased burn.

OKC.name: Chet Holmgren
OKC.note: Holmgren underwent a biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear and will miss at least 8-10 weeks, Nick Crain of Slam reports.
OKC.long: This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

OKC.name: Jalen Williams
OKC.note: Williams (leg) underwent successful surgery Wednesday to "address a fractured left fibula and reconstruction of ankle ligaments following a fracture and dislocation." He will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Tim MacMahon of ESPN.com reports.
OKC.long: Williams suffered the injury during Sunday's meeting with the Clippers and was taken off the court on a stretcher. It's unknown when the 25-year-old will be cleared to return, though the Thunder will presumably be overly cautious moving forward. Williams, who signed a five-year extension in July of 2025, has had a productive career, averaging 17.9 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.3 steals over 30.9 minutes per contest. However, after playing at least 69 regular-season games in his first three years in the league, he has appeared in just 36 in the last two seasons combined. With the Thunder having one of the deepest rosters in the NBA, the team may look for more minutes from Jared McCain, Jaylin Williams, and Kenrich Williams for the remainder of the 2026-27 campaign.

ORL.name: Desmond Bane
ORL.note: Bane (illness) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Warriors.
ORL.long: Bane will miss Saturday night's contest in Golden State with an illness. He joins Paolo Banchero (ankle) and Jalen Suggs (knee) on the sidelines, as the Magic now have 60 percent of their opening night starting lineup donning street clothes. Bane's next chance to suit up will come Tuesday versus the Kings. In his absence, expect Jase Richardson, Jamal Cain and Jevon Carter to absorb extra minutes.

ORL.name: Jonathan Isaac
ORL.note: Orlando recalled Isaac (knee) from the G League's Osceola Magic on Wednesday.
ORL.long: Isaac was assigned to Osceola but recalled again on the same day while he continued his recovery from a knee issue. Having yet to play this season, the forward is not expected to find a meaningful role in the short term, and he'll likely appear on the bench when he's available again.

ORL.name: Jalen Suggs
ORL.note: Suggs has been diagnosed with a mild bone bruise in his right knee and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
ORL.long: Suggs suffered the injury during Sunday's win over the Knicks when his right knee buckled following a layup attempt. Fortunately, further testing revealed no major structural damage, though the 25-year-old will miss at least two weeks before being re-evaluated. Anthony Black and Jase Richardson could see increased opportunities in Orlando's backcourt during Suggs' absence.

ORL.name: Paolo Banchero
ORL.note: Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
ORL.long: Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

ORL.name: Noah Penda
ORL.note: Penda was diagnosed with a partially torn right hamstring Saturday, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
ORL.long: Penda suffered the hamstring tear in Friday's 136-115 preseason win over the Heat. It's unknown how long the injury will keep the 21-year-old off the floor. However, since it's a different injury than the one he suffered in the same hamstring during training camp, the team may take a cautious approach regarding his return. Penda, the No. 32 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, averaged 3.8 points, 3.2 rebounds and 1.2 assists over 12.8 minutes per outing in 59 regular-season games in 2025-26. While he's not expected to be a mainstay in the rotation throughout the 2026-27 campaign, his absence could open up a few minutes for Tristan Da Silva.

ORL.name: Izaiyah Nelson
ORL.note: Team president Jeff Weltman said Monday that Nelson (ankle) remains about a month away from returning to the court after offseason surgery, per Philip Rossman-Reich of OrlandoMagicDaily.com.
ORL.long: With Nelson still in recovery mode from the left ankle surgery he underwent this summer, his path back to game action remains delayed for the early part of the season. The rookie big man is on a two-way contract with the Magic, so his short-term absence mainly affects his developmental timeline rather than Orlando's regular rotation.

PHI.name: Adem Bona
PHI.note: Bona (back) is out for Sunday's game in Chicago.
PHI.long: Bona will miss his second straight game Sunday, which should again result in some extra minutes for Jabari Walker. Bona's next chance to play will come Tuesday against the Celtics.

PHI.name: Dominick Barlow
PHI.note: Head coach Nick Nurse said Wednesday that Barlow (back) likely needs another 10-12 days before he's cleared to return to the court, Derek Bodner of AllPHLY.com reports.
PHI.long: Nurse added that the team is "pretty positive" that Barlow's back is getting better, though he's still going to have to wait some more time before being cleared. The big man has yet to make his season debut due to a lumbar spine bone stress response, and he isn't expected to return until mid-November at the earliest.

PHI.name: Ariel Hukporti
PHI.note: Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
PHI.long: Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

PHX.name: Jordan Goodwin
PHX.note: Goodwin (calf) is questionable for Monday's game against the Spurs.
PHX.long: Goodwin could miss a fourth straight game due to a right calf injury. Collin Gillespie and Luke Kennard are likely to retain expanded roles if Goodwin is unable to go.

PHX.name: Mark Williams
PHX.note: Williams underwent surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss an extended period of time, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
PHX.long: This is a tough blow for the center with training camp right around the corner. With his status for Opening Night in jeopardy, this will put a lot of eyes on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach, with the latter already drawing buzz during the Summer League. More clarity on Williams' timeline should be known in the coming weeks.

POR.name: Robert Williams III
POR.note: Williams (rest) won't play in Saturday's game against the Spurs.
POR.long: Williams logged 16 minutes in Friday's 124-118 loss to the Lakers, though he won't play Saturday versus San Antonio, the second game of a back-to-back for Portland. As a result, Branden Carlson and Yang Hansen should each receive more playing time behind Donovan Clingan.

POR.name: Ja Morant
POR.note: Head coach Micah Nori said Morant met with a doctor in Los Angeles, who gave him a positive outlook on his recovery from the hamstring injury. While Nori declined to update Morant's timetable, he added Morant "may not be out for as long as we thought," Trail Blazers Insider Sean Highkin reports.
POR.long: Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

POR.name: Vit Krejci
POR.note: Head coach Micah Nori said that Krejci suffered a left leg fracture during Wednesday's 132-119 win over the Suns, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
POR.long: Nori did not provide a timetable for Krejci, but it's safe to say that he won't be back soon. His minutes figure to be divvied up amongst Chris Youngblood and Sidy Cissoko.

POR.name: Shaedon Sharpe
POR.note: Sharpe suffered a torn meniscus in his knee and is expected to miss six months, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
POR.long: It's a tough blow to the Trail Blazers' depth on the wing ahead of training camp. Sharpe, who is now likely to be sidelined until after the All-Star break, had been ticketed for a reserve role behind Toumani Camara following an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign, which saw average a career-high 20.8 points, 1.4 steals and 2.1 three-pointers per game over 50 regular-season appearances. The door is now open for Vit Krejci and Jeremy Sochan to compete for bench minutes during camp.

SAC.name: Domantas Sabonis
SAC.note: Sabonis (knee) is out for Sunday's game against the Heat.
SAC.long: Sabonis was a late addition to the injury report due to left knee soreness, and he will be unavailable for Sunday's contest. Dylan Cardwell and Precious Achiuwa are candidates for increased playing time in his absence.

SAC.name: Maxime Raynaud
SAC.note: Raynaud (knee) is progressing in his rehabilitation and will be re-evaluated in approximately two weeks, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
SAC.long: Raynaud's absence is expected to extend into mid-November due to a right patellar subluxation. With Dylan Cardwell (calf) set to miss at least one more week, Precious Achiuwa, Jonathan Mogbo and De'Andre Hunter are candidates for increased minutes in the frontcourt.

SAC.name: Ben Simmons
SAC.note: Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
SAC.long: Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

SAS.name: Tobias Harris
SAS.note: Harris (calf) is listed as out for Monday's game against Phoenix.
SAS.long: Harris is almost cleared to suit up. However, he won't play Monday versus the Suns, meaning his next chance to make his 2026-27 campaign debut will come Wednesday in Chicago.

SAS.name: Devin Vassell
SAS.note: Vassell is questionable for Monday's game against the Suns due to left adductor tightness.
SAS.long: Vassell could miss his first game this season. If he is unable to go, Julian Champagnie, Keldon Johnson and Carter Bryant could see extra minutes.

SAS.name: Jayden Quaintance
SAS.note: Quaintance has been around the team but has not yet been cleared for basketball activities, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
SAS.long: The Spurs are expected to exercise extreme caution with the big man, as Quaintance suffered a torn ACL and meniscus with Arizona State in February 2025 before appearing in only four games with Kentucky last season due to severe complications and persistent swelling. The 19-year-old underwent a cleanup procedure on his meniscus in mid-July, and the Spurs will likely want him at 100 percent before ramping him up to basketball activities.

TOR.name: Nate Bittle
TOR.note: Bittle (foot) is listed as out for Monday's game against Memphis.
TOR.long: Bittle has been battling a foot injury for a couple of months. It's unknown when the rookie will be cleared to suit up for the Raptors, so he should be considered week-to-week for now.

TOR.name: Immanuel Quickley
TOR.note: Quickley (hamstring) was a limited participant in Sunday's practice and will be listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Grizzlies, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports.
TOR.long: Quickley is in danger of missing a second consecutive contest due to a right hamstring injury. If the 27-year-old point guard remains sidelined, Jamal Shead and Alijah Martin would be candidates for increased playing time.

TOR.name: Scottie Barnes
TOR.note: Barnes (adductor) was a limited participant in Sunday's practice and will be listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Grizzlies, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports.
TOR.long: Barnes was held out of Friday's win over Milwaukee and could miss a second straight game due to left adductor soreness. If the star forward remains on the inactive list alongside Kawhi Leonard (knee), Collin Murray-Boyles, Allen Graves and Jamison Battle would be candidates for increased playing time.

TOR.name: Kawhi Leonard
TOR.note: Leonard has completed treatment to reduce swelling in his left knee and he will be re-evaluated in one week, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
TOR.long: Leonard will now begin the next phase of his rehab, and while he'll be re-evaluated by Nov. 10, it's still unlikely we'll see him back on the floor until the end of November. Ja'Kobe Walter should continue to start while Leonard is sidelined, and it'll be Scottie Barnes, Immanuel Quickley and RJ Barrett running the show on offense.

UTA.name: Lauri Markkanen
UTA.note: Markkanen (wrist) is out for Sunday's game against the Timberwolves, Shreyas Laddha of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
UTA.long: Markkanen will miss Sunday's game due to a right wrist injury he sustained Oct. 26 against the Grizzlies. Josh Green, Josh Okogie and Brice Sensabaugh are candidates for increased roles with Markkanen sidelined.

UTA.name: Keyonte George
UTA.note: George will not return to Sunday's game against the Timberwolves due to a right ankle injury.
UTA.long: George suffered a right ankle injury during the fourth quarter of Sunday's game and will not return. He concludes the contest with 19 points (5-13 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 9-10 FT), eight assists, five rebounds and two steals in 29 minutes. George should be considered questionable for Tuesday's game against the Heat.

UTA.name: Jusuf Nurkic
UTA.note: Nurkic (toe) has begun participating in on-court activities as he continues recovering from a right foot injury sustained during an Oct. 4 preseason game against Denver. He will be re-evaluated in two weeks, the Jazz announced Friday.
UTA.long: Nurkic is progressing in his recovery, but the two-week re-evaluation timeline indicates he remains some distance from returning to game action. His absence should continue to create opportunities in Utah's frontcourt, with Jaxson Hayes and Mo Bamba among the players positioned to benefit from additional playing time. Nurkic's next evaluation will provide a clearer picture of his potential return date.

UTA.name: Jaren Jackson Jr.
UTA.note: Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
UTA.long: Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.

WAS.name: Tristan Vukcevic
WAS.note: Vukcevic (hip) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Detroit.
WAS.long: Vukcevic has yet to make his season debut due to a left hip impingement. The big man can be viewed as week-to-week until the Wizards provide an update on his progress.

WAS.name: Anthony Davis
WAS.note: Davis (ankle) is listed as questionable for Monday's game in Detroit.
WAS.long: Davis has missed the last two games. It appears he has a chance to return Monday against the Pistons. However, if Davis isn't cleared to suit up for that contest, Bilal Coulibaly could remain in the starting lineup. Deandre Ayton (leg), who is not listed on the injury report, is also a candidate to start.

WAS.name: Reece Beekman
WAS.note: The Wizards announced Monday that Beekman sustained a right acromioclavicular joint injury and will be re-evaluated in approximately three weeks.
WAS.long: Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.

WAS.name: Justin Champagnie
WAS.note: Champagnie (foot) is expected to miss several months, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic.
WAS.long: The forward underwent surgery Wednesday to address a fractured foot, and the Wizards hope Champagnie will be ready to return at some time around the All-Star break in February. The likes of Bilal Coulibaly, Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington will all be asked to help pick up the slack for the foreseeable future.

WAS.name: Jamir Watkins
WAS.note: The Wizards announced Thursday that Watkins has undergone surgery for a torn ACL.
WAS.long: Watkins, a two-way player for the Wizards, suffered the injury during the Summer League. Although Washington has yet to offer a timetable for a return, a typical recovery time for the procedure is approximately 9-to-12 months. That leaves Watkins in serious jeopardy of missing most, if not all, of the 2026-27 season, and it remains to be seen if the team will continue keeping him around on a two-way roster spot while he's injured.
